newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says regrets S.Africa's China move.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says regrets S.Africa's China move.

text.p: Taiwan said on Thursday it regretted an "extremely unfriendly decision" by South Africa, the island's biggest diplomatic partner, to sever ties in favour of Taiwan's arch rival, communist China.

"This action seriously hurts the friendly relationship between the two countries," Foreign Ministry spokesman Peter Cheng told reporters at a late-night news conference. "For this extremely unfriendly decision we express our regret."
Cheng indicated that Taipei felt the decision was not final, calling on Pretoria to reverse it and vowing to seek talks with the South African government over the matter.

"The South African government should cherish the friendly relationship between the two countries and seriously reconsider this decision," he said. "We are continuing to try to understand all developments there."
President Nelson Mandela said on Wednesday South Africa would move to shift recognition to Beijing from Taipei over the space of a year, with completion at the end of 1997.

The move strips Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government of biggest diplomatic ally and will leave the Nationalist-ruled island recognised by only 29 states, mostly poor countries in Central America and Africa that depend on Taiwan for aid.
